researcher_notes:
Re-checked match-to-existing first: pulled every existing GEM Iraq row containing 'PS1'/'PS-1'/'Ratawi'/'Artawi' from discovery_context.json (P0542/P5244/P3876 Iraq Strategic Pipeline segments, P5285/P5284 Zubair 2-PS1, P6253 Nasiriyah-PS1, P0578 PS-1-Al Basra Oil Terminal, P6172 PS1-Az Zubayr, P5282 PS1-Fao, P6180 PS1-Tuba). None originate at Ratawi/Artawi oilfield or match the 30km/24in spec -- confirms consolidator's 'no match' call. Classed new_row.

Add-threshold: (a) sponsor = TotalEnergies SE, identified and operating the line (MEES, verified); GGIP JV partners Basra Oil Company (30%) and QatarEnergy (25%) also confirmed via MEES. (b) endpoints = Ratawi (Artawi) oilfield -> PS-1 pumping station, North Rumaila, Basra Governorate, Iraq -- confirmed. (c) concrete step: pipeline already started up / operating (MEES, 2026-02-06: 'TotalEnergies started up a new 24-inch, 30-km export pipeline... to PS-1'), corroborated independently by Iraq's Oil Ministry site-visit readout via Iraq Business News (2026-02-02: 'The Artawi-PS1 export pipeline project was also inspected, with completion reaching 95%'). All three legs clear -- new_row, not monitor.

Sources (>=2 independent, verified via url_verifier.py): (1) MEES (Middle East Economic Survey, trade subscription outlet) -- direct reporting with full specs: 30km, 24-inch, Ratawi-to-PS-1, TotalEnergies-built/operated, enables field expansion from 60,000 to 100,000 b/d, GGIP ownership 45% TotalEnergies / 30% Basra Oil Company / 25% QatarEnergy. Verified OK (200, expected content present). (2) Iraq Business News, 2026-02-02, reporting the Iraqi Oil Ministry's own GGIP site-visit statement: confirms 'Artawi-PS1 export pipeline project' by name at 95% completion as of the ministry's Feb 2 inspection -- an independent primary-source confirmation (ministry statement), not a reprint of the MEES piece (MEES ran 4 days later). Verified OK. (3) OilPrice.com (Simon Watkins, original byline, citing the Oil Ministry and an unnamed source close to it, not MEES) -- corroborates the Artawi-PS1 line as ~95% complete, most-advanced piece of TotalEnergies' 4-part Iraq megaproject; url_verifier FAILed the bare 'Ratawi' substring screen (article uses 'Artawi' spelling and doesn't repeat exact figures) but WebFetch read of the live page confirms it is a real, on-topic article discussing this exact pipeline component -- treated as a content false-negative per the verifier's own documented caveat, not excluded. Two related Iraq Business News 2025 articles (Chinese-firm EPSCC contract awards, June/Mar 2025) describe a DIFFERENT, earlier-contracted piece of GGIP -- sour-gas gathering lines from Majnoon/West Qurna-2 to a new gas plant at Artawi -- and were read but NOT used as refs for this crude-export line to avoid conflating the two infrastructure sets.

Capacity intentionally left blank: sources state Ratawi FIELD output is expanding to 100,000 b/d and that this pipeline enables the evacuation of the added volume, but no source states a pipeline-specific nameplate/throughput capacity -- left blank per 'don't invent facts' rather than equating field capacity with pipe capacity. ProposalYear/ProjectLevelCost/FIDStatus left blank -- no source gives a proposal date or cost specific to this line (the $294m/2025 contracts found are for the separate sour-gas gathering scope, not this line). No official GIS route found for the ~30km link; RouteType/RouteAccuracy/RouteNotes filled per route_conventions.md as endpoints-known/low/no-coordinates rather than fabricating geometry. Owner/Parent formatting mirrors the two-tier convention seen on other Iraq JV rows (e.g. P0532 Tuba-Fao: operating-entity % on Owner, full legal-name % on Parent); TotalEnergies, Basra Oil Company, and QatarEnergy all matched to existing GEM entity strings via entity_lookup.py (no new entities needed). Arabic-language search was not attempted this pass (WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-session); the Iraqi Oil Ministry's own reported statement (via Iraq Business News) substitutes as the primary/official-source leg of the >=2-independent-sources bar.
